$comment: Mirror map + coverage inventory for the backend/board <-> frontend/lib/board pair
(openspec: cross-stack-determinism, requirement 'Shared Board Math Is Pinned By a
Cross-Language Golden Fixture'). Names EVERY function defined in both mirrors,
whether or not exported on either side. Rewritten with the polar board
(rewrite-board-on-polar-lattice, 2026-08-25): the hex-era pairs (Line, RouteAround,
axial/cube machinery, hexDirection/angleDelta, layoutConstants' sqrt3) left with the
hex lattice; lib/hex is renamed lib/board.
Enforced by .claude/scripts/check-mirror-map.sh (wired into /check): every top-level
production function extracted from either package must appear here (in 'pairs',
'goOnly', or 'tsOnly'), and every pair must be covered by a fixture family in
fixtures/board/cases.json or listed in 'inventory' with the change expected to cover
it. The extractor sees `func` / `function` declarations; if a mirrored arrow-function
const is ever added to lib/board, extend the extractor to match.
coverage values: 'family:<name>' — asserted by that fixture family (directly, or
indirectly as a callee of the family's function; indirect coverage is imperfect by
nature); 'inventory' — no family exercises it, tracked as a gap below. A rule-bearing
pair SHALL NOT remain in the inventory across more than one change that modifies its
package. The pinned coordinate table itself is asserted byte-identical by both
suites (the cases file's 'coordinateTable' object records its digest); the loader
pairs below claim indirect coverage through the geometry families that read it.

indirect (the BFS frontier under every distance case and sweep)
indirect (the folded coast's period pins the orbital law); names differ across the seam
indirect (the mid-burn shipPos cases interpolate through it — the integer round-half-up index)
indirect (the settled coast's boundary snap — the fixture pins both snap directions)
indirect (every gate case asserts the returned cell's ring)
indirect (the argmax's float dot product — the discretized-choice seam; Go inhibits FMA with explicit conversions, JS rounds each op separately)
indirect (every visibility/beam/gate computation reads pinned centers through it; the table itself is byte-identity-asserted by both suites)
indirect (the pinned-table loader — loads committed data, never recomputes)

unassigned (canonical (ring, slot) projection; asserted by unit tests on both sides)
the consumer-migration change (rule-bearing: lane position/fraction reads; may not survive another board-modifying change uncovered)
